text: A service can be 18% faster, or 8% slower but keep operating through a single local failure. Assume the expected yearly value is otherwise similar. Which default do you prefer?
Two projects have similar expected value. A has 25% more upside but depends on one external partner; B has lower upside but you control the critical path. Which would you rather own?
You must choose today. A 30-minute diagnostic has a 20% chance of changing the decision, but waiting carries a small real cost. What is your default?

options.text: Decide now and accept the uncertainty

text: A critical workflow can use one highly optimized path, or two independent paths that cost 12% more to maintain. Both meet current demand. Which architecture do you prefer?
Option A gives a modest advantage immediately but is hard to reverse for a year. Option B gives up that advantage but can be changed next month. Which feels stronger?

You can maintain one strategy tuned very well to the current environment, or three meaningfully different strategies that each perform slightly worse today. Future conditions are uncertain but not chaotic. Which do you choose?

The same policy works well in most contexts but underperforms in one stable subgroup. A single universal rule is simpler; a context-specific rule is slightly harder to maintain. Which default do you prefer?

options.text: Use a context-specific rule for the subgroup

text: A pipeline slows down. Component metrics show one module is slightly noisier, while handoff latency between modules also rose slightly. You can investigate only one first. Which do you pick?
A model is still useful but repeatedly misses one bounded regime. You can patch that regime now, or keep the simpler model until the miss causes a larger operational cost. Which do you prefer?

options.text: Keep the simpler model for now

text: Strategy A has about 12% higher expected return, but a 1% annual event could erase most accumulated gains. Strategy B removes that tail event but loses the 12% edge. Which is your default?

A team has one hour to act. The objective is broadly understood but not numerically specified. Do you spend the first 10 minutes defining the success metric, or start execution and refine the metric from feedback?

options.text: Start execution and refine from feedback

text: A quick check costs almost nothing and catches 55% of faults; a full diagnostic catches 95% but delays action by two hours. The current fault is inconvenient, not dangerous. Which do you run first?
A repeated pattern strongly suggests X may drive Y, but a clean causal test will take a week. A reversible intervention based on X can start today. What do you prefer?

options.text: Wait for the cleaner causal test

text: Two simple rules each work well in different regimes. A regime detector is 85% accurate. Would you keep one simpler global rule or combine the detector with both rules?
One high-quality new result conflicts with a stable older body of evidence. You have time for only one audit pass before deciding what to do next. Which direction do you prioritize?

options.text: Stress-test the new result against the old body
Use the new result to stress-test the assumptions behind the old body

text: An update improves 92% of users and harms 8%. You can either roll it back for everyone immediately or keep it live while isolating the affected subgroup for a targeted fix. The harm is real but reversible. Which do you choose?

options.text: Keep it live and isolate the 8%

text: A promising signal is based on a small sample. Waiting for more evidence means missing a short window of opportunity; acting now is reversible but costs resources. Which default fits you better?

options.text: Act now because the move is reversible

text: Two plans have similar expected value. Plan A is more focused and easier to manage; Plan B keeps three future branches open but requires extra coordination now. Which do you prefer?
A team misses targets. Individual performance varies moderately, and coordination overhead has also grown. You can change only one thing this week. Which intervention do you prefer first?
You have spare budget for one improvement: either add 20% peak capacity to the main path, or build a smaller independent fallback that handles only 40% of normal load. Which do you fund?
